title: Underclassman
full_review:
"Underclassman" (Miramax) flunks out as entertainment.

Set in Los Angeles, the lightweight action comedy stars Nick Cannon as Tracy "Tre" Stokes, an impetuous but streetwise rookie cop tired of pedaling a beat as a member of the LAPD's beach bike patrol.

Against the better judgment of his police captain (Cheech Marin), the youthful-looking Tre is assigned to pose undercover as a student (a la "21 Jump Street") at a silver-spoon academy in order to investigate the murder of a student.

Culture-shock complications ensue as he befriends the lead suspect, well-heeled jock Rob Donovan (Shawn Ashmore), but Tre manages to uncover a ring of car thieves and drug dealers operating on campus.

Clumsily directed by Marcos Siega, the formulaic fish-out-of-water film aspires to be a high-school version of "Beverly Hills Cop," but Cannon lacks Eddie Murphy's comic charm and much of the flat script's humor relies on racial stereotyping.

So far this summer, Siega is 0 for 2 with films having to do with nasty rich kids, having also directed the raunchy teen satire "Pretty Persuasion." And while it is the more watchable of the two, "Underclassman" is, in a word, underwhelming.

The film has recurring action violence, teenage drinking, drug content, sexual references and innuendo and brief potty humor, as well as sporadic crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
